daily_report_items: Accepted the medium-confidence, medium-sensitivity positive beneficiary relationship from the defense and aerospace replenishment cycle to RTX based on defense backlog, Raytheon program growth and margin expansion, and group cash generation; no strategy follow-up was created because commercial diversification, Pratt remediation, contract execution, leverage, overbought conditions, and adverse valuation remain unresolved.

evidence.claim: RTX reported USD 289 billion of total backlog at 30 June 2026, including USD 119 billion of defense backlog, with USD 8.305 billion of cash and USD 37.383 billion of total debt. The filing supports current backlog, segment economics, cash flow, balance-sheet, fixed-price contract risk, and Pratt powder-metal remediation analysis.

RTX reported Q2 2026 sales of USD 24.7 billion and USD 3.5 billion of operating cash flow; Raytheon sales rose 18%, adjusted operating margin rose to 12.6% from 11.6%, and full-year free-cash-flow guidance increased to USD 8.50-8.75 billion.

The maintained idea defines the causal path from funded allied procurement and replenishment through awards, qualified production, deliveries, sustainment, margin, and cash flow, while requiring contract, capacity, supplier, export, and valuation confirmation.

The maintained RTX review records direct Raytheon defense exposure and improving segment economics, but both bounded valuation scenarios remain below the USD 218.42 mark and commercial aerospace, engine remediation, leverage, and execution risks block a strategy.
